cues.en: What you're looking at right now is something called quaternion multiplication,
cues.zh: 你现在看到的东西叫做四元数乘法，

cues.en: or rather you're looking at a certain representation
cues.zh: 更准确地说，你看到的是某种表示方式，

cues.en: of a specific motion happening on a four dimensional sphere being represented in our three-dimensional
cues.zh: 它表示一个发生在四维球面上的特定运动，如何呈现在我们的三维

cues.en: space,
cues.zh: 空间中，

cues.en: one which you'll understand by the end of this video.
cues.zh: 看完这个视频，你就会明白它。

cues.en: Quaternions are an absolutely fascinating and often underappreciated
cues.zh: 四元数是数学中一个绝对迷人、却常被低估的

cues.en: number system from math.
cues.zh: 数系。

cues.en: Just as complex numbers are a two dimensional extension of the real numbers, quaternions are a four dimensional extension of complex numbers.
cues.zh: 正如复数是实数在二维上的扩展，四元数是复数在四维上的扩展。

cues.en: But they're not just playful mathematical shenanigans.
cues.zh: 但它们可不只是好玩的数学把戏。

cues.en: They have a surprisingly pragmatic utility for describing rotation in three dimensions and even for quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 它们在描述三维旋转方面有出奇实用的价值，甚至在量子力学中也有用。

cues.en: The story of their discovery is also quite famous in math. The Irish mathematician William Rowan Hamilton spent much of his life seeking a three-dimensional number system analogous to the complex numbers.
cues.zh: 它们被发现的故事在数学界也相当有名。爱尔兰数学家 William Rowan Hamilton 大半生都在寻找一个类似于复数的三维数系。

cues.en: And as the story goes, his son would ask him every morning whether or not he had figured out how to divide triples, and he would always say, no. Not yet. But on 10/16/1843,
cues.zh: 据说，他的儿子每天早上都会问他有没有想出如何做三元数除法，而他总是说，没有，还没有。但在 1843 年 10 月 16 日，

cues.en: while crossing the Broome Bridge in Dublin, he realized with a supposed flash of insight that what he needed was not to add a single dimension to the complex numbers,
cues.zh: 当他走过都柏林的 Broome Bridge 时，他灵光一闪，意识到他需要的并不是给复数增加一个维度，

cues.en: but to add two more imaginary dimensions,
cues.zh: 而是增加两个虚数维度，

cues.en: three imaginary dimensions describing space
cues.zh: 三个描述空间的虚数维度

cues.en: and the real numbers sitting perpendicular to that in some kind of fourth dimension.
cues.zh: 以及与之垂直的实数，位于某种第四维中。

cues.en: He carved the crucial equation describing these three imaginary units into the bridge, which today bears a plaque in his honor showing that equation.
cues.zh: 他把描述这三个虚数单位的关键方程刻在桥上；今天那座桥上有一块纪念他的铭牌，展示着这个方程。

cues.en: Now you have to understand, our modern notion of vectors with their dot product and the cross product and things like that didn't really exist in Hamilton's time, at least not in a standardized form. So after his discovery, he pushed hard for quaternions to be the primary language with which we teach students to describe three-dimensional space, even forming an official quaternion
cues.zh: 你得明白，我们现代关于向量、点积、叉积之类的概念，在 Hamilton 的时代其实并不存在，至少没有标准化的形式。所以在他发现之后，他极力推动让四元数成为我们教学生描述三维空间的主要语言，甚至成立了一个官方的四元数

cues.en: society to proselytize his discovery.
cues.zh: 协会，来宣传他的发现。

cues.en: Now, unfortunately,
cues.zh: 然而不幸的是，

cues.en: this was balanced with mathematicians on the other side of the fence who believed that the confusing notion of quaternion multiplication was not necessary for describing three dimensions,
cues.zh: 与之相抗衡的是另一派数学家，他们认为四元数乘法这种令人困惑的概念对描述三维空间并不必要，

cues.en: resulting in some truly hilarious old timey trash talk legitimately calling them evil.
cues.zh: 结果产生了一些非常搞笑的旧时代垃圾话，甚至真的称它们为邪恶。

cues.en: It's even believed that the Mad Hatter scene from Alice in Wonderland, whose author you may know was an Oxford mathematician,
cues.zh: 甚至有人认为，《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的疯帽匠场景——你可能知道作者是牛津数学家——

cues.en: was written in reference to quaternions,
cues.zh: 是在影射四元数，

cues.en: that the chaotic table placement changes were mocking their multiplication,
cues.zh: 混乱的餐桌摆放变化是在嘲讽它们的乘法，

cues.en: and that certain quotes were referencing their noncommutative
cues.zh: 而某些台词则是在指涉它们的非交换

cues.en: nature.
cues.zh: 性质。

cues.en: Fast forward about a century, and the computing industry gave quaternions a resurgence among programmers who work with graphics and robotics and anything involving orientation in three d space.
cues.zh: 快进约一个世纪，计算机工业让四元数在从事图形学、机器人学以及任何涉及三维空间朝向的程序员中重新流行起来。

cues.en: And this is because they give an elegant way to describe and to compute three d rotations,
cues.zh: 因为它们提供了一种优雅的方式来描述和计算三维旋转，

cues.en: which is computationally more efficient than other methods and which also avoids a lot of the numerical errors that arise in these other methods. The twentieth century also brought quaternions some more love from a completely different direction, quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 这在计算上比其他方法更高效，也避免了这些其他方法中出现的许多数值误差。二十世纪还从完全不同的方向——量子力学——给四元数带来了更多青睐。

cues.en: You see, the special actions that quaternions describe in four dimensions are actually quite relevant to the way that two state systems, like spin of an electron or the polarization of a photon, are described mathematically.
cues.zh: 你看，四元数在四维中描述的特殊作用，其实与二态系统（比如电子自旋或光子偏振）在数学上的描述方式相当相关。

cues.en: What I'll show you here is a way to visualize quaternions in their full four dimensional glory.
cues.zh: 这里我要展示的，是一种把四元数完整的四维全貌可视化出来的方法。

cues.en: It would surprise me if this approach was fully original, but I can say that it's certainly not the standard way to teach quaternions
cues.zh: 如果这个方法完全原创，我会很惊讶；但我可以说，它绝不是教四元数的标准方式，

cues.en: and that the specific four dimensional right hand rule image that I'd like to build up to is something that I haven't really seen elsewhere.
cues.zh: 而且我最终想构建的那个具体四维右手定则图景，是我在别处没怎么见过的。

cues.en: Building up an understanding for this visual will take us meaningful time, but once you have it, there is a very natural and satisfying intuition for how to think about quaternion multiplication.
cues.zh: 理解这个可视化要花我们不少时间，但一旦掌握，就会对如何思考四元数乘法有一种非常自然且令人满足的直觉。

cues.en: It won't be until the next video that I show you how exactly quaternions describe orientation in three dimensions, which is, for some people, the whole reason we care about it. But once we're able to go at it armed with the image of what they're doing to a four d hypersphere,
cues.zh: 要到下一个视频，我才会展示四元数究竟如何描述三维中的朝向——对一些人来说，这正是我们关心它的全部原因。但一旦我们带着“它们对四维超球面做了什么”的图景去攻克它，

cues.en: there's a pleasing understanding to be had for the otherwise opaque formulas characterizing
cues.zh: 对于那些本来晦涩、用来刻画

cues.en: this relationship.
cues.zh: 这种关系的公式，也能收获一种令人愉快的理解。

cues.en: The structure here will be to start by imagining teaching complex numbers to someone who only understands one dimension,
cues.zh: 这里的安排是：先设想向一个只理解一维的人讲授复数，

cues.en: then describing three d rotations to someone who only understands two dimensions,
cues.zh: 然后向一个只理解二维的人描述三维旋转，

cues.en: and ultimately to represent what quaternions are doing up in four dimensions within the constraints of our three d space.
cues.zh: 最终在我们三维空间的限制下，表示四元数在四维中到底在做什么。

cues.en: Our first character is Linus the lionlander whose mind can only grasp the one dimensional geometry of lines and the algebra of real numbers. We're gonna try to describe complex numbers to Linus, and it's really important for you to empathize with him as much as you can during this because in a few minutes, you're gonna be in his shoes.
cues.zh: 我们的第一个角色是 Linus the lionlander，他的头脑只能理解直线的一维几何和实数的代数。我们将试着向 Linus 描述复数；在这个过程中，你尽可能设身处地理解他，这非常重要，因为几分钟后，你就会站在他的位置。

cues.en: On the one hand, you could define complex numbers purely algebraically.
cues.zh: 一方面，你可以纯代数地定义复数。

cues.en: You say each one is expressed as some real number plus some other real number times I,
cues.zh: 你会说，每个复数都表示成某个实数加上另一个实数乘以 I，

cues.en: where I is a newly invented constant whose defining property is that I times I equals negative one.
cues.zh: 其中 I 是一个新发明的常数，其定义性质是 I 乘 I 等于负一。

cues.en: Then you say to Linus, to multiply two complex numbers, you just use the distributive property, what many people learn in school as foil.
cues.zh: 然后你告诉 Linus，要计算两个复数相乘，只需用分配律，也就是很多人在学校学过的 FOIL 法则。

cues.en: And you apply this rule that I times I equals negative one to simplify things down further.
cues.zh: 接着利用 i 乘以 i 等于 -1 这条规则进一步化简。

cues.en: And that's fine. That totally works, and the standard textbook way to introduce quaternions is analogous to this, showing the algebraic rules and calling it done. But I think something is missing if we don't at least try to show Linus the geometry of complex numbers and what complex multiplication looks like since the problems in math and physics where complex numbers are shockingly useful often leverage this spatial intuition.
cues.zh: 这样没问题，完全行得通，教科书介绍四元数的标准做法也类似——摆出代数规则就算完事了。但如果我们不试着向 Linus 展示复数的几何意义以及复数乘法究竟长什么样，我觉得就缺少了灵魂，因为在数学和物理中，复数之所以惊人地好用，往往正是借助了这种空间直觉。

cues.en: You and I, who understand two dimensions, might think of it like this. When you multiply two complex numbers, z times w, you can think of z as a sort of function acting on w, rotating and stretching it in some way.
cues.zh: 理解二维空间的你我可能会这样想：当计算复数乘法 z 乘以 w 时，可以把 z 看作作用在 w 上的某种函数，对它进行某种旋转和拉伸。

cues.en: I like to think of this by broadening the view and asking what does z do to the entire plane? And you can think of that bird's eye view action by imagining using one hand to fix the number zero in place and using another hand to drag the point at one up to z since anything times zero is zero and anything times one is itself.
cues.zh: 我喜欢放宽视野来思考：z 对整个平面做了什么？你可以从俯瞰视角来想象这个操作：一手固定住数字 0，另一手把点 1 拖动到 z 的位置，因为任何数乘 0 都是 0，乘 1 则保持不变。

cues.en: And in two dimensions, there is one and only one stretching rotating action on the plane that'll do this. This is also how I'll have you thinking about quaternion multiplication later on, where the number on the left acts as a kind of function to the one on the right. And we'll understand this function by seeing how it acts by transforming space.
cues.zh: 在二维空间中，有且仅有一种平面的拉伸旋转操作能做到这一点。后面讲四元数乘法时，我也会带大家用这种方式思考：左边的数充当作用在右边数上的某种函数。我们将通过观察它如何变换空间来理解这个函数。

cues.en: Although instead of rotating two d space, it does a sort of double rotation in four d space.
cues.zh: 只不过它不是旋转二维空间，而是在四维空间中进行某种双重旋转。

cues.en: By the way, if you want to review thinking about complex numbers as a kind of action, a good warm up for this video might be the one I did on e to the pi I explained with introductory group theory.
cues.zh: 顺便提一句，如果你想重温“把复数看作一种作用”的思路，可以看看我之前用群论入门解释 e 的 πi 次方那个视频，那是个很好的预热。

cues.en: Now Linus the line lander is pretty comfortable with the idea of stretching. That's what multiplication by real numbers looks like. Maybe it's a little weird for him to think about stretching in multiple dimensions, but it's not fundamentally different. The difficult thing to communicate to Linus is rotation.
cues.zh: 生活在线段国的 Linus 对拉伸的概念已经很熟悉了，实数乘法就是这样的。多维度的拉伸对他来说可能有点奇怪，但本质上没有区别。真正难向 Linus 传达的是旋转。

cues.en: Specifically, focus on the unit circle of the complex plane, all the numbers a distance one from zero, since multiplication by these numbers corresponds to pure rotation.
cues.zh: 具体来说，可以聚焦在复平面的单位圆上，也就是所有到 0 距离为 1 的数，因为乘以这些数对应的就是纯旋转。

cues.en: How would you explain to Linus the look and the feel of multiplying by these numbers?
cues.zh: 你要如何向 Linus 解释乘以这些数的直观感受呢？

cues.en: At first, that might seem impossible. I mean, rotation is just such an intrinsically two dimensional idea.
cues.zh: 乍一听这似乎不可能。毕竟，旋转完全是一个本质上属于二维的概念。

cues.en: But on the other hand, rotation involves only one degree of freedom. A single number, the angle, specifies a given rotation uniquely.
cues.zh: 但另一方面，旋转只涉及一个自由度。一个数——角度——就能唯一确定一个给定的旋转。

cues.en: So in principle, it should be possible to associate the set of all rotations to the one dimensional continuum that is Linus' world.
cues.zh: 所以原则上，应该可以把所有旋转的集合，对应到 Linus 世界中的一维连续统上。

cues.en: And there are many ways you could do this, but the one I'm gonna show you is what's called a stereographic projection.
cues.zh: 做这件事有很多方法，但我要给你们看的这种方法叫球极投影。

cues.en: It's a special way to map a circle onto a line or a sphere into a plane or even a four d hypersphere into three d space.
cues.zh: 它是一种特殊的方式，可以把圆映射到直线，把球面映射到平面，甚至把四维超球面映射到三维空间。

cues.en: For every point on the unit circle, draw a line from negative one through that point, and wherever it intersects the vertical line through the circle's center, that's where the point of the circle gets projected.
cues.zh: 对单位圆上的每个点，从 -1 出发画一条穿过该点的直线，它与穿过圆心的竖线相交的位置，就是这个圆上点的投影位置。

cues.en: So for example, the point at one gets projected into the center of the line.
cues.zh: 例如，点 1 会被投影到这条线的中心。

cues.en: The point I actually stays fixed in place as does negative I.
cues.zh: 点 i 实际上保持不动，-i 也一样。

cues.en: All of the points on that 90 degree arc between one and I will get projected somewhere in the interval between where one landed and where I landed.
cues.zh: 从 1 到 i 之间那段 90 度弧上的所有点，都会投影到 1 的落点和 i 的落点之间的某个区间里。

cues.en: As you continue farther around the circle on the arc between I and negative one, the projected points end up farther and farther away at an increasing rate.
cues.zh: 当你沿着 i 和 -1 之间的弧继续绕圆走得更远，投影点会落在越来越远的位置，而且距离增长越来越快。

cues.en: Similarly, if you come around the other way towards negative one, the projected points end up farther and farther on the other end of the line.
cues.zh: 同样，如果你从另一个方向绕向 -1，投影点会落到直线另一端越来越远的位置。

cues.en: This line of projected points is what we show to Linus, labeling a few key points, like one and I and negative one all for reference.
cues.zh: 我们给 Linus 看的就是这条由投影点组成的直线，并标出几个关键点，比如 1、i 和 -1，作为参照。

cues.en: Technically, the point at negative one has no projection under this map since the tangent line to the circle at that point never crosses the vertical line. But what we say is that negative one ends up at the point at infinity.
cues.zh: 严格来说，-1 这个点在这种映射下没有投影，因为该点处圆的切线永远不会与竖线相交。但我们会说，-1 最终落在无穷远点。

cues.en: This is a special point you imagine adding to the line where you would approach it if you walk infinitely far along the line in either direction.
cues.zh: 这是一个特殊的点，你可以想象把它加到直线上；沿直线往任一方向走无限远，都会趋近它。

cues.en: Now it's important to remember and to remind Linus that what he's seeing is only the complex numbers that are a distance one from the origin, the unit circle. Linus doesn't see most numbers like zero or one plus I or negative two minus I, but that's okay because right now we just wanna describe complex number z where multiplying by z has the effect of a pure rotation,
cues.zh: 现在要记住，也要提醒 Linus：他看到的只是到原点距离为 1 的那些复数，也就是单位圆。Linus 看不到大多数数，比如 0、1+i 或 -2-i，但这没关系，因为现在我们要描述的是复数 z，乘以 z 的效果是纯旋转，

cues.en: so he only needs to understand the unit circle.
cues.zh: 所以他只需要理解单位圆。

cues.en: For example, when we take the number I and multiply it by any other complex number w, the effect is to rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise.
cues.zh: 例如，当我们取数 i 并乘以任意其他复数 w 时，效果就是逆时针旋转 90 度。

cues.en: And when we apply this action to the circle being projected down to the line for Linus, what does he see?
cues.zh: 把这个作用施加到为 Linus 投影到直线上的圆上，他会看到什么？

cues.en: Well, it's a bit of a strange morphing action on the line, one which I want you to become familiar with for something we'll see later on. It's easiest to understand by following a few key reference points.
cues.zh: 嗯，这是直线上一种有点奇怪的变形作用，我希望你们先熟悉它，因为后面我们会看到相关的东西。要理解它，最简单的方法是跟踪几个关键参考点。

cues.en: I times one is I, so that means the number one should move up to I.
cues.zh: I 乘以 1 等于 I，这意味着数字 1 应该向上移动到 I。

cues.en: I times I is negative one, so the point at I slides off to infinity.
cues.zh: I 乘以 I 等于负 1，所以 I 处的那个点会滑向无穷远。

cues.en: I times negative one is equal to negative I, so that point at infinity kind of comes back around from the bottom to the position one unit below the center.
cues.zh: I 乘以负 1 等于负 I，所以无穷远处的那个点就像是从底部绕回来，移动到中心下方一个单位的位置。

cues.en: And I times negative I is one,
cues.zh: 而 I 乘以负 I 等于 1，

cues.en: so that point at negative I slides up to one.
cues.zh: 所以负 I 处的点会向上滑动到 1。

cues.en: Even though this is kind of a weird motion, it lets us communicate some important ideas to Linus.
cues.zh: 虽然这种运动看起来有点奇怪，但它能让我们向 Linus 传达一些重要概念。

cues.en: For example, multiplying by I four times, which corresponds to rotating by 90 degrees four times in a row, gets us back to where we started.
cues.zh: 例如，连续乘以 I 四次，对应连续旋转 90 度四次，会让我们回到起点。

cues.en: I to the fourth equals one.
cues.zh: I 的四次方等于 1。

cues.en: Here, to get more of a feel for things, let me just show the circle rotated at various different angles. On both the left and the right half of the screen here, I'm putting a hand on the point that started at the number one to help us and to help Linus keep track of the overall motion.
cues.zh: 为了让大家有更直观的感受，我来展示一下圆在不同角度下的旋转。在屏幕的左半部分和右半部分，我都在起始于数字 1 的点上放了一只手，帮助我们和 Linus 追踪整体的运动。

cues.en: Next, let's introduce Felix the flatlander who only understands two dimensional geometry.
cues.zh: 接下来，让我们介绍只能理解二维几何的平面人 Felix。

cues.en: Imagine trying to explain rotations of a sphere to Felix.
cues.zh: 想象一下要如何向 Felix 解释球体的旋转。

cues.en: In the spirit of transitioning from complex numbers to quaternions,
cues.zh: 本着从复数过渡到四元数的思路，

cues.en: let's extend the complex numbers with its horizontal axis of real numbers and its vertical axis of imaginary numbers with a third axis defined by some newly invented constant, j, sitting one unit away from zero perpendicular to the complex plane.
cues.zh: 复数原本包含实数横轴和虚数纵轴，我们在此基础上扩展出第三条轴，它由新引入的常数 j 定义，垂直于复平面且距离原点一个单位。

cues.en: Instead of having this new axis in the z direction like you might expect, for a better analogy with how we'll visualize quaternions,
cues.zh: 与其像你预期的那样把这条新轴放在 z 轴方向，为了更好地类比我们后续对四元数的可视化，

cues.en: we'll want to orient things so that the I and the j axes
cues.zh: 我们希望调整方向，让 I 轴和 j 轴

cues.en: sit in the x and the y directions
cues.zh: 分别位于 x 和 y 方向，

cues.en: with the real number line aligned along the z direction.
cues.zh: 而实数轴则沿着 z 方向排列。

cues.en: So every point in three d space is described as some real number plus some real number times I plus some real number times j.
cues.zh: 这样一来，三维空间中的每个点都可以表示为：某个实数 + 某个实数乘 I + 某个实数乘 j。

cues.en: As it happens, it's not possible to define a notion of multiplication for a three d number system like this that would satisfy the usual algebraic properties that make multiplication a useful construct. Perhaps I'll outline why this is the case in a follow on video, but staying focused on our current goal, think about describing three d rotations in this coordinate system to Felix the Flatlander.
cues.zh: 然而事实证明，我们无法为这样的三维数系定义乘法，使其满足让乘法产生实用价值的常规代数性质。也许我会在后续视频中概述其中的原因，但专注于我们当前的目标，先想想该怎么在这个坐标系中向平面人 Felix 描述三维旋转。

cues.en: The unit sphere consists of all those numbers which are a distance one from zero at the origin,
cues.zh: 单位球面由所有距离原点 0 为 1 的数组成，

cues.en: meaning the sum of the squares of their coordinates is one.
cues.zh: 也就是各坐标的平方和等于 1。

cues.en: We can't show all of three d space to Felix, but what we can do is project this two d surface to him and give him a feel for what reorientations of the sphere look like under that projection.
cues.zh: 我们无法向 Felix 展示完整的三维空间，但我们可以把这个二维曲面投影给他看，让他感受一下在这种投影下球体的旋转朝向是什么样的。

cues.en: Analogous to what we did before, stereographic projection will associate almost every point on the unit sphere with a unique point on the horizontal plane defined by the I and the j axes.
cues.zh: 和之前类似，球极投影会把单位球面上的几乎每个点，与由 I 轴和 j 轴定义的水平平面上的唯一一点对应起来。

cues.en: For each point on the sphere, draw a line from negative one at the South Pole through that point and see where it intersects the plane.
cues.zh: 对球面上的每个点，从南极的 -1 出发，经过该点画一条直线，看它与平面相交在哪里。

cues.en: So the point one at the North Pole ends up at the center of the plane. All of the points of the Northern Hemisphere get mapped somewhere inside the unit circle of the I j plane.
cues.zh: 于是北极的 1 会落到平面中心。北半球的所有点都会被映射到 I-j 平面单位圆内的某个位置。

cues.en: And that unit circle, which passes through I j negative I negative j, actually stays fixed in place.
cues.zh: 而这个单位圆，经过 I、j、-I、-j，实际上保持不动。

cues.en: And that's an important point to make note of. Even though most points and lines and patches that Felix the Flatlander sees are gonna be warped projections of the real sphere, this unit circle is the one thing that he has which is an honest part of our unit sphere, unaltered by projection.
cues.zh: 这一点很重要。虽然平面人 Felix 看到的大多数点、线和区域，都是真实球面经过扭曲后的投影，但这个单位圆是他看到的唯一一个真正属于我们单位球面、且未被投影改变的东西。

cues.en: All of the points in the Southern Hemisphere get projected outside that unit circle, each getting farther and farther away as you approach negative one at the South Pole.
cues.zh: 南半球的所有点都会被投影到那个单位圆外；越接近南极的 -1，它们就离得越远。

cues.en: And, negative one has no projection under this mapping, but what we say is that it ends up at some point at infinity.
cues.zh: 而 -1 在这个映射下没有投影，不过我们可以说它最终落在某个无穷远点。

cues.en: That point at infinity is something such that no matter which direction you walk on the plane, as you go infinitely far out, you'll be approaching that point. It's analogous to how if you walk any direction away from the North Pole, you're approaching the South Pole.
cues.zh: 这个无穷远点的意思是：无论你在平面上朝哪个方向走，只要走到无限远，就会趋近于那个点。这类似于：从北极朝任意方向走远，都会趋近南极。

cues.en: Now let me just pull up a view of what Felix sees in two dimensions.
cues.zh: 现在我来调出 Felix 在二维中看到的视图。

cues.en: As I rotate the sphere in various ways, the lines of latitude and longitude drawn on that sphere get projected into various circles and lines in Felix's space. And the way I've done things up here, the checkerboard pattern on the surface of this sphere is accurately reflected in the projected view that you see with Felix. And the pink dot represents where the point that started at the North Pole ends up after the rotation.
cues.zh: 当我以各种方式旋转球面时，球面上画出的纬线和经线会被投影成 Felix 空间中的各种圆和直线。按照我这里的设置，这个球面上的棋盘格图案会准确反映在你看到的 Felix 投影视图中。粉色点表示最初在北极的那个点在旋转后落到了哪里。

cues.en: And that yellow circle represents where the equator ended up after the projection.
cues.zh: 那个黄色圆表示赤道经过投影后到了哪里。

cues.en: The more you put yourself in Felix's shoes right now, the easier quaternions be in a moment. And as with Linus, it helps to focus on a few key reference objects rather than trying to see the whole sphere.
cues.zh: 你现在越能站在 Felix 的角度看，待会儿理解四元数就越容易。和 Linus 那时一样，专注于几个关键参照物，比试图看清整个球面更有帮助。

cues.en: This circle passing through one, I, negative one, and negative I gets mapped onto a line which Felix sees as the horizontal axis.
cues.zh: 这个经过 1、I、-1 和 -I 的圆，会被映射成一条直线，而 Felix 把它看作水平轴。

cues.en: It's important to remind Felix that what he sees is not the same thing as the I axis. Remember, we're only projecting the numbers that have a distance one from the origin. So most points on the actual I axis, like zero and two I and three I, etcetera, are completely invisible to Felix.
cues.zh: 要提醒 Felix：他看到的东西并不等同于 I 轴。记住，我们只投影到原点距离为 1 的那些数。所以真实 I 轴上的大多数点，比如 0、2I、3I 等等，对 Felix 来说完全不可见。

cues.en: Similarly,
cues.zh: 类似地，

cues.en: the circle that passes through one, j, negative one, and negative j gets projected onto what he sees as a vertical line.
cues.zh: 穿过 1、j、-1 和 -j 的圆，被投影成了他眼中的一条竖线。

cues.en: And in general, any line that Felix sees comes from some circle on the sphere that passes through negative one.
cues.zh: 一般来说，Felix 看到的任何直线，都来自球面上穿过 -1 的某个圆。

cues.en: In some sense, a line is just a circle that passes through the point at infinity.
cues.zh: 在某种意义上，直线就是一个穿过无穷远点的圆。

cues.en: Now think about what Felix sees as we rotate the sphere.
cues.zh: 现在想想看，当我们旋转球面时，Felix 会看到什么。

cues.en: A 90 degree rotation about the j axis brings one to I, I to negative one, negative one to negative I, and negative I to one.
cues.zh: 绕 j 轴旋转 90 度，会把 1 变成 i，i 变成 -1，-1 变成 -i，-i 变成 1。

cues.en: So what Felix the flatlander sees is an extension of the rotation that Linus the line lander was seeing.
cues.zh: 所以二维扁平人 Felix 看到的，正是线段人 Linus 所见旋转的扩展。

cues.en: Notice also that this action rotates the I j unit circle to the position where the one j unit circle used to be. So what Felix sees is his yellow unit circle getting transformed into a vertical line,
cues.zh: 还要注意，这一操作将 i-j 单位圆旋转到了原来 1-j 单位圆所在的位置。所以在 Felix 看来，他的黄色单位圆变成了一条竖线，

cues.en: while that red vertical line gets transformed into the unit circle.
cues.zh: 而那条红色竖线则变成了单位圆。

cues.en: Of course, from our perspective, we know this is all just rigid motion. No actual stretching or morphing is taking place. All of that is just an artifact of the projection.
cues.zh: 当然，在我们看来，这只是一次刚体运动。根本没有发生真正的拉伸或形变，这一切都只是投影产生的假象。

cues.en: Similarly, a rotation about the I axis involves moving one to j, j to negative one, negative one to negative j, and negative j to one.
cues.zh: 类似地，绕 i 轴旋转意味着将 1 变为 j，j 变为 -1，-1 变为 -j，-j 变为 1。

cues.en: This rotation turns the I j unit circle into the one I unit circle, which to Felix looks like the unit circle getting transformed into a horizontal line.
cues.zh: 这次旋转把 i-j 单位圆变成了 1-i 单位圆，在 Felix 眼中就像是单位圆变成了一条水平线。

cues.en: A rotation about the real axis is actually quite easy for Felix to understand since the whole projection simply gets rotated about the origin, where the only points staying fixed in place are one at the origin and negative one off at infinity.
cues.zh: 绕实轴旋转对 Felix 来说其实很好理解，因为整个投影只是绕着原点旋转，唯二固定不动的点只有原点处的 1 和无穷远处的 -1。

cues.en: In the same way that the complex numbers included the real numbers with a single extra, quote, unquote, imaginary dimension
cues.zh: 正如复数在实数的基础上增加了一个所谓的“虚数”维度，

cues.en: represented by the unit I,
cues.zh: 由单位 i 来表示，

cues.en: and that the not actually a number system thing we had in three dimensions included a second imaginary direction, j, The quaternions include the real numbers together with three separate imaginary dimensions represented by the units I, j, and k.
cues.zh: 而我们在三维中讨论过的那个“并非真正数系”的结构包含了第二个虚数方向 j，四元数则包含实数以及三个独立的虚数维度，分别由单位 i、j 和 k 表示。

cues.en: Each of these three imaginary dimensions is perpendicular to the real number line, and they're all perpendicular to each other somehow.
cues.zh: 这三个虚数维度都垂直于实数线，而且它们彼此之间也以某种方式相互垂直。

cues.en: So in the same way that complex numbers are represented as a pair of real numbers, each quaternion can be written using four real numbers, and it lives in four dimensional space.
cues.zh: 因此，就像复数由一对实数表示一样，每个四元数都可以用四个实数来表示，并且存在于四维空间中。

cues.en: You often think of this as being broken up into a real or scalar part and then a three d imaginary part. And Hamilton used a special word for quaternions that had no real part and just I j k components, a word which was previously somewhat foreign in the lingo of math and physics, vector.
cues.zh: 通常可以把它拆分为一个实数或标量部分，加上一个三维虚部。对于没有实部、只有 i、j、k 分量的四元数，Hamilton 用了一个特殊的词来称呼，这个词在当时的数学和物理学术语中还颇为生僻：向量（vector）。

cues.en: On the one hand, you could just define quaternion multiplication by giving the rules for how I, j, and k multiply together and saying that everything must distribute nicely.
cues.zh: 一方面，你可以直接定义四元数乘法：给出 i、j、k 之间的相乘规则，并规定必须满足分配律。

cues.en: This is analogous to defining complex multiplication by saying that I times I is negative one and then distributing and simplifying products.
cues.zh: 这类似于定义复数乘法：规定 i 乘以 i 等于负一，然后展开并化简结果。

cues.en: And indeed, this is how you would tell a computer to perform quaternion multiplication.
cues.zh: 实际上，你让计算机执行四元数乘法时就是这么实现的。

cues.en: And the relative compactness of this operation compared to say matrix multiplication
cues.zh: 相比于矩阵乘法等操作，这种运算相对更加紧凑，

cues.en: is what's made quaternion so useful for graphics programming and many other things.
cues.zh: 这正是四元数在图形学编程等众多领域大显身手的原因。

cues.en: There's also a rather elegant form of this multiplication rule written in terms of the dot product and the cross product. And in some sense, quaternion multiplication
cues.zh: 这种乘法规则还有一种相当优雅的形式，可以用点积和叉积来表示。从某种意义上说，四元数乘法

cues.en: subsumes both of these notions, at least as they appear in three dimensions.
cues.zh: 涵盖了这两种概念，至少涵盖了它们在三维空间中的表现形式。

cues.en: But just as a deeper understanding for complex multiplication
cues.zh: 但正如对复数乘法更深刻的理解

cues.en: comes from understanding its geometry,
cues.zh: 来源于对其几何意义的认识——

cues.en: that multiplying by a complex number involves a combination of scaling and rotating, you and I are here for the four dimensional geometry of quaternion multiplication.
cues.zh: 乘以一个复数本质上是缩放和旋转的结合，今天我们要探究的正是四元数乘法的四维几何本质。

cues.en: And just as the magnitude of a complex number, its distance from zero, is the square root of the sum of the squares of its component,
cues.zh: 正如复数的模长（也就是到零点的距离）等于各分量平方和的平方根一样，

cues.en: that same operation gives you the magnitude of a quaternion.
cues.zh: 完全相同的运算也能得出四元数的模长。

cues.en: And multiplying one quaternion, q one, by another, q two,
cues.zh: 用一个四元数 q1 乘以另一个四元数 q2，

cues.en: has the effect of scaling q two by the magnitude of q one followed by a very special type of rotation in four dimensions.
cues.zh: 其效果是先将 q2 缩放 q1 的模长倍，接着在四维空间中进行一种非常特殊的旋转。

cues.en: And those special four d rotations, the heart of what we need to understand,
cues.zh: 而那些特殊的四维旋转——我们要理解的核心——

cues.en: correspond to the hypersphere of quaternions,
cues.zh: 对应着四元数的超球面，

cues.en: a distance one from the origin,
cues.zh: 即到原点距离为 1 的球面，

cues.en: both in the sense that the quaternions whose multiplying action is a pure rotation live on that hypersphere
cues.zh: 一方面是因为乘法作用为纯旋转的四元数都落在这个超球面上，

cues.en: and in the sense that we can understand this weird four d action just by following points on the hypersphere rather than trying to look at all of the points in the inconceivable stretches of four dimensional space.
cues.zh: 另一方面，我们只需观察超球面上的点，就能理解这种奇特的四维变换，而不必去硬看那令人难以想象的辽阔四维空间中的所有点。

cues.en: Analogous to what we did for Linus and Felix, we stereographically
cues.zh: 类似于我们为 Linus 和 Felix 所做的那样，我们通过球极投影

cues.en: project this hypersphere into three d space.
cues.zh: 将这个超球面投影到三维空间中。

cues.en: This label in the upper right is gonna show a given unit quaternion,
cues.zh: 右上角的标签会显示一个给定的单位四元数，

cues.en: and this little pink dot will show where that particular quaternion
cues.zh: 而这个粉色小点则表示该四元数

cues.en: gets projected in our three d space.
cues.zh: 投影在我们三维空间中的位置。

cues.en: Just as before, we're projecting from the number negative one, which sits on the real number line that is somehow perpendicular
cues.zh: 和之前一样，我们从数字负一处进行投影，它位于实数轴上，而这条实数轴垂直于

cues.en: to all of our three d space and beyond our perception. Perception.
cues.zh: 我们整个三维空间，超出了我们的感知。感知。

cues.en: Just as before, the number one ends up projected straight into the center of our space.
cues.zh: 同样和之前一样，数字 1 最终被直接投影到了我们空间的中心。

cues.en: And in the same way that I and negative I were fixed in place for Linus and that the I j unit circle was fixed in place for Felix,
cues.zh: 正如对 Linus 而言 i 和负 i 位置固定，对 Felix 而言 ij 单位圆位置固定一样，

cues.en: we get a whole sphere passing through I j and k on that unit hypersphere,
cues.zh: 我们在那个单位超球面上得到了一个穿过 i、j、k 的完整球面，

cues.en: which stays in place under the projection.
cues.zh: 它在投影后依然保持不动。

cues.en: So what we see as a unit sphere in our three d space represents the only unaltered part of the hypersphere of quaternions getting projected down onto us. It's something analogous to the equator of a three d sphere, and it represents all of the unit quaternions whose real part is zero, what Hamilton would have described as unit vectors.
cues.zh: 我们在三维空间中看到的单位球面，代表了四元数超球面投影下来时唯一没有形变的部分。它类似于三维球面的赤道，代表所有实部为零的单位四元数，也就是 Hamilton 所称的单位向量。

cues.en: The unit quaternions with positive real parts between zero and one end up somewhere inside this unit sphere, closer to the number one in our three d space, which should feel analogous to how the Northern Hemisphere got mapped inside the unit circle for Felix.
cues.zh: 实部在 0 到 1 之间的正实部单位四元数，最终会落在单位球面内的某个位置，在三维空间中离 1 更近，这类似于 Felix 视角下北半球被映射到单位圆内部的方式。

cues.en: On the other hand, all the unit quaternions with negative real part end up somewhere outside that unit sphere.
cues.zh: 另一方面，所有实部为负的单位四元数最终都落在该单位球面外部的某处。

cues.en: The number negative one is sitting off at the point at infinity, which you can easily find by walking in any direction.
cues.zh: 数字 -1 则处在无穷远点，朝任意方向走都能轻松找到它。

cues.en: Keep in mind, even though we see the projection of some of these quaternions as being closer or farther from the origin of our three d space, everything you're looking at represents a unit quaternion.
cues.zh: 请记住，虽然我们看到某些四元数的投影离三维空间的原点更近或更远，但你眼前看到的这一切代表的都是单位四元数。

cues.en: So everything you're looking at really has the same magnitude,
cues.zh: 所以你看到的一切其实模长都是相同的，

cues.en: the same distance from the number zero.
cues.zh: 离数字 0 的距离也完全一样。

cues.en: And that number zero itself is nowhere to be found in this picture. Like all other non unit quaternions,
cues.zh: 而数字 0 本身在这个画面中是找不到的。就像所有其他非单位四元数一样，

cues.en: it's invisible to us.
cues.zh: 它对我们来说是隐形的。

cues.en: In the same way that for Felix, the circle passing through one, I, negative one, and negative I got projected into a line through the origin,
cues.zh: 就像在 Felix 眼中，穿过 1、i、-1 和 -i 的圆被投影成了一条穿过原点的直线一样，

cues.en: when we see this line through the origin passing through I and negative I, we should understand that it really represents a circle.
cues.zh: 当我们看到这条穿过原点且经过 i 和 -i 的直线时，就应该明白它实际上代表一个圆。

cues.en: Likewise, up on the hypersphere, invisible to us, there is a unit sphere
cues.zh: 同样，在对我们隐形的超球面上，存在一个单位球面，

cues.en: passing through one I j, negative one, negative I, and negative j. And that whole sphere gets projected into the plane that we see passing through one I, negative I, j, negative j, and negative one off at infinity, what you and I might call the x y plane.
cues.zh: 它穿过 1、i、j、-1、-i 和 -j。而整个球面被投影到我们看到的平面上，穿过 1、i、-i、j、-j 以及无穷远处的 -1，也就是你我常说的 xy 平面。

cues.en: In general, any plane that you see here really represents the projection of a sphere somewhere up on the hypersphere which passes through the number negative one.
cues.zh: 一般而言，你在这里看到的任何平面，实际上都代表超球面上穿过数字 -1 的某个球面的投影。

cues.en: Now the action of taking a unit quaternion
cues.zh: 现在，取一个单位四元数，

cues.en: and multiplying it by any other quaternion from the left can be thought of in terms of two separate two d rotations happening perpendicular to and in sync with each other in a way that could only ever be possible in four dimensions.
cues.zh: 并用任何其他四元数从左边乘它，这种操作可以理解为两个相互垂直且同步发生的独立二维旋转，这种运动只有在四维空间中才有可能实现。

cues.en: As a first example, let's look at multiplication by I.
cues.zh: 作为第一个例子，我们来看乘以 i。

cues.en: We already know what this does to the circle that passes through one and I, which we see as a line.
cues.zh: 我们已经知道它对穿过 1 和 i 的圆（即我们看到的直线）有什么影响。

cues.en: One goes to I,
cues.zh: 1 变成 i，

cues.en: I goes to negative one, half at infinity,
cues.zh: i 变成无穷远处的 -1，

cues.en: Negative one comes back around to negative I, and negative I goes to one. Remember, just like what Linus saw, all of this is the stereographic
cues.zh: -1 绕回来变成 -i，而 -i 则变成 1。别忘了，就像 Linus 看到的一样，这一切都是

cues.en: projection of a 90 degree rotation.
cues.zh: 90 度旋转的立体投影。

cues.en: Now look at the circle passing through j and k, which is in a sense perpendicular to the circle passing through one and I.
cues.zh: 现在来看穿过 j 和 k 的圆，它在某种意义上垂直于穿过 1 和 i 的圆。

cues.en: Now it might feel weird to talk about two circles being perpendicular to each other, especially when they have the same center, the same radius, and they don't touch each other at all, but nothing could be more natural in four dimensions.
cues.zh: 谈论两个圆互相垂直可能感觉很怪，尤其是它们同心、等半径，而且完全不相交，但在四维空间中，这再自然不过了。

cues.en: You can think of the action of I on this perpendicular circle as obeying a certain right hand rule.
cues.zh: 你可以把 i 在这个垂直圆上的作用，理解为遵循某种右手定则。

cues.en: If you'll excuse the intrusion of my ghostly green screen hand into our otherwise pristine platonic mathematical stage,
cues.zh: 请原谅我这只绿幕幽灵手突兀地伸进了原本纯粹的柏拉图数学舞台，

cues.en: you let that thumb of your right hand point from the number one to I, and you curl your fingers.
cues.zh: 让你的右手大拇指从数字 1 指向 i，然后弯曲四指。

cues.en: The j k circle will rotate in the direction of that curl.
cues.zh: j-k 圆就会沿着四指弯曲的方向旋转。

cues.en: How much? Well, by the same amount as the one I circle rotates, which is 90 degrees in this case.
cues.zh: 转多少呢？和 1-i 圆转动的幅度一样，在这里就是 90 度。

cues.en: This is what I meant by two rotations perpendicular to and in sync with each other.
cues.zh: 这就是我说的两个互相垂直且步调一致的旋转。

cues.en: So j goes to k,
cues.zh: 于是 j 变到了 k，

cues.en: k goes to negative j,
cues.zh: k 变到了 -j，

cues.en: negative j goes to negative k,
cues.zh: -j 变到了 -k，

cues.en: and negative k goes to j.
cues.zh: -k 变到了 j。

cues.en: This gives us a little table for what the number I does to the other quaternions.
cues.zh: 这就给出了数字 i 对其他四元数作用的小对照表。

cues.en: But I want this not to be something that you memorize, but something that you could close your eyes and you could really see.
cues.zh: 但我希望大家不要死记硬背，而是闭上眼睛就能真正看清这个画面。

cues.en: Computationally,
cues.zh: 从计算上来说，

cues.en: if you know what a quaternion does to the numbers one, I, j, and k,
cues.zh: 如果你知道一个四元数对数字 1、i、j、k 的作用，

cues.en: you know what it does to any arbitrary quaternion since multiplication
cues.zh: 你就能知道它对任意四元数的作用，因为乘法

cues.en: distributes nicely.
cues.zh: 满足良好的分配律。

cues.en: In the language of linear algebra, one, I, j, and k form a basis of our four dimensional space,
cues.zh: 用线性代数的语言来说，1、i、j、k 构成了四维空间的一组基，

cues.en: so knowing what our transformation does to them gives us the full information about what it does to all of space.
cues.zh: 所以知道变换对它们的作用，就掌握了变换对整个空间作用的全部信息。

cues.en: Geometrically,
cues.zh: 从几何上来说，

cues.en: a four dimensional creature would be able to look at those two perpendicular rotations that I just described and understand that they lock you into one and only one rigid motion for the hypersphere.
cues.zh: 一个四维生物只要看到我刚才描述的那两个互相垂直的旋转，就能明白它们确定了超球面上唯一的一种刚体运动。

cues.en: We might lack the intuitions of such a hypothetical creature, but we can maybe try to get close.
cues.zh: 我们可能缺乏这种假想生物的直觉，但或许可以试着靠近一些。

cues.en: Here's what the action of repeatedly multiplying by I looks like on our stereographic projection of the I j k sphere.
cues.zh: 这就是连续乘以 i 在 i-j-k 球面的立体投影上看起来的样子。

cues.en: It gets rotated into what we see as a plane, then gets rotated further back to where it used to be, though the orientation is all reversed now.
cues.zh: 它先旋转成我们看到的平面，然后进一步转回原来的位置，不过方向完全反过来了。

cues.en: Then it gets rotated again into what we see as a plane, and after the fourth iteration, it ends up right back where it started.
cues.zh: 接着它再次旋转成一个平面，在第四次迭代之后，彻底回到了最初的起点。

cues.en: As another example, think of a quaternion like q equals negative square root of two over two plus square root of two over two times I,
cues.zh: 再举个例子，考虑一个四元数，比如 q 等于负二分之根号二加上二分之根号二乘以 i，

cues.en: which if we pull up a picture of a complex plane, is a 135
cues.zh: 如果我们调出复平面的图像，这代表一个 135

cues.en: degree rotation away from one in the direction of I.
cues.zh: 度的旋转，从 1 朝着 i 的方向转过去。

cues.en: Under our projection, we see this along the line from one to I somewhere outside the unit sphere.
cues.zh: 在我们的投影下，可以看到它位于从 1 到 i 的直线上，处于单位球面外的某处。

cues.en: If that sounds weird, just remember how Linus would have seen the same number.
cues.zh: 如果这听起来很怪，不妨想想 Linus 会怎样看待同一个数。

cues.en: The action of multiplying this q by all other quaternions
cues.zh: 用这个 q 去乘以所有其他四元数的作用，

cues.en: will look to us like dragging the point at one all the way to this projected version of q,
cues.zh: 在我们看来，就像把 1 处的点一路拖到 q 的这个投影位置，

cues.en: while the j k circle gets rotated a 135 degrees according to our right hand rule.
cues.zh: 同时 jk 圆按照我们的右手定则旋转 135 度。

cues.en: Multiplication by any other quaternion
cues.zh: 乘以任何其他四元数

cues.en: is completely similar. For example, let's see what it looks like for j to act on other quaternions by multiplication from the left.
cues.zh: 过程都完全类似。例如，我们来看看用 j 从左侧乘以其他四元数会是什么样子。

cues.en: The circle through one and j, which we see projected as a line through the origin, gets rotated 90 degrees, dragging one up to j. So j times one is one, and j times j is negative one.
cues.zh: 穿过 1 和 j 的圆（在投影中显示为穿过原点的直线）旋转了 90 度，把 1 拖到了 j。所以 j 乘以 1 等于 j，而 j 乘以 j 等于 -1。

cues.en: The circle perpendicular to that one passing through I and k gets rotated 90 degrees according to this right hand rule where you point your thumb from one to j. So j times I is negative k,
cues.zh: 与之垂直且穿过 i 和 k 的圆，按照大拇指从 1 指向 j 的右手定则旋转 90 度。所以 j 乘以 i 等于 -k，

cues.en: and j times k is I.
cues.zh: 而 j 乘以 k 等于 i。

cues.en: In general, for any other unit quaternion you see somewhere in space, start by drawing the unit circle passing through one, q, and negative one, which we see in our projection as a line through the origin.
cues.zh: 一般来说，对于你在空间中看到的任意其他单位四元数，先画出穿过 1、q 和 -1 的单位圆，在投影中它表现为一条穿过原点的直线。

cues.en: Then draw the circle perpendicular to that one on what we see as the unit sphere.
cues.zh: 然后在我们看到的单位球面上，画出与它垂直的那个圆。

cues.en: You rotate the first circle so that one ends up where q was and rotate the perpendicular circle by the same amount according to the right hand rule.
cues.zh: 旋转第一个圆，让 1 落在 q 原本的位置，并根据右手定则将垂直的圆旋转相同的角度。

cues.en: One thing worth noticing here is that order of multiplication matters.
cues.zh: 这里值得注意的一点是，乘法的顺序至关重要。

cues.en: It's not, as mathematicians would say, commutative.
cues.zh: 用数学家的话说，它不满足交换律。

cues.en: For example, I times j is k, which you might think of in terms of I acting on the quaternion j rotating it up to k.
cues.zh: 例如，i 乘以 j 等于 k，你可以理解为 i 作用在四元数 j 上，把它旋转到了 k。

cues.en: But if you think of j is acting on I, j times I,
cues.zh: 但如果是 j 作用在 i 上，即 j 乘以 i，

cues.en: it rotates I to negative k.
cues.zh: 它会把 i 旋转到 -k。

cues.en: In fact, commutativity,
cues.zh: 事实上，可交换性，

cues.en: this ability to swap the order of multiplication,
cues.zh: 也就是随意调换乘法顺序的能力，

cues.en: is a way more special property than a lot of people realize.
cues.zh: 远比许多人意识到的要特殊得多。

cues.en: And most groups of actions on some space don't have it. It's like how in solving a Rubik's cube, order matters a lot.
cues.zh: 大多数作用在空间上的群都不具备这种性质。就像解魔方时，操作顺序极其关键一样。

cues.en: Or how rotating a cube about the z axis and then about the x axis gives a different final state from rotating it about the x axis then about the z axis.
cues.zh: 又比如，将立方体先绕 z 轴再绕 x 轴旋转，与先绕 x 轴再绕 z 轴旋转，得到的最终状态截然不同。

cues.en: And last, as one final but rather important point, so far I've shown you how to think about quaternions as acting by left multiplication,
cues.zh: 最后还有一个相当重要的要点：到目前为止，我展示的都是把四元数看作“左乘”操作，

cues.en: where when you read an expression like I times j, you think of I as a kind of function morphing all of space, and j is just one of the points that it's acting on. But you can also think of them as a different sort of action by multiplying from the right, where in this expression, j would be acting on I.
cues.zh: 当你看到像 i 乘以 j 这样的表达式时，会把 i 看作变换整个空间的某种函数，而 j 只是被作用的点之一。但你也可以把它看作另一种“右乘”操作，在此时的表达式中，就变成了 j 作用于 i。

cues.en: In that case, the rule for multiplication is very similar. It's still the case that one goes to j and j goes to negative one, etcetera.
cues.zh: 那样的话，乘法规则也非常相似。仍然是 i 变成 j，j 变成 -i，等等。

cues.en: But instead of applying the right hand rule to the circle perpendicular to the one j circle, you would use your left hand.
cues.zh: 但这时不是对垂直于 i-j 圆的那个圆应用右手定则，而是用左手。

cues.en: So either way, I times j is equal to k, but you can either think about this with your right hand curling the number j to the number k as your thumb points from one to I,
cues.zh: 所以无论哪种方式，i 乘 j 都等于 k；你可以用右手把 j 卷向 k，同时让拇指从 i 指向 k，

cues.en: or as your left hand curling I to k as its thumb points from one to j.
cues.zh: 或者用左手把 i 卷向 k，同时让拇指从 i 指向 j。

cues.en: Understanding this left hand rule for multiplication from the other side will be extremely useful for understanding how unit quaternions
cues.zh: 从另一侧理解这个左手乘法规则，对理解单位四元数如何

cues.en: describe rotation in three dimensions.
cues.zh: 描述三维旋转，会非常有用。

cues.en: And so far, it's probably not clear how exactly quaternions do describe three rotation. I mean, if you consider one of these actions on the unit sphere passing through I, j, and k, it doesn't leave that sphere in place. It morphs it out of position. So the way that this works is slightly more complicated than a single quaternion product.
cues.zh: 到目前为止，可能还不太清楚四元数究竟如何描述三维旋转。我的意思是，如果你考虑单位球面上经过 i、j、k 的某个作用，它并不会让球面保持原位，而是会把它移出位置。所以它的工作方式比单次四元数乘法稍微复杂一些。

cues.en: It involves a process called conjugation, and I'll make a full follow on video all about it so that we have the time to go through some examples.
cues.zh: 它涉及一个叫共轭的过程，我会做一个完整的后续视频专门讲它，这样我们就有时间过一些例子。

cues.en: In the meantime, for more information on the story of quaternions and their relation to orientation in three d space,
cues.zh: 与此同时，想了解更多四元数的故事及其与三维空间取向的关系，

cues.en: Quanta, a mathematical publication I'm sure a lot of you are familiar with, just put out a post in a kind of loose conjunction with this video. Link in the description.
cues.zh: Quanta——我确定很多观众都熟悉的数学刊物——刚刚配合这个视频发布了一篇文章。链接在描述里。

cues.en: If you enjoyed this, consider sharing it with some friends. And if you felt like the narrative structure here was actually helpful for understanding,
cues.zh: 如果你喜欢，可以考虑分享给朋友。如果你觉得这里的叙事结构确实有助于理解，

cues.en: maybe reassure those friends who would be turned off by a large time stamp that good math is actually worth the time.
cues.zh: 也许可以安慰那些会被长时间戳劝退的朋友：好数学其实值得花时间。

cues.en: And many thanks to the patrons among you. I actually spent way longer than I care to admit on this project, so your patience and support is especially appreciated this time around.
cues.zh: 也多谢你们的赞助者。这个项目我花的时间远超我愿意承认，所以这次尤其感谢你们的耐心和支持。
